dependencies.basis: FJP's own 'PIB dos Municipios Mineiros 2019' states municipal GDP is calculated by Brazil's Sistema de Contas Regionais, coordinated by IBGE in partnership with state statistical institutes -- naming Fundacao Joao Pinheiro as Minas Gerais's institute -- and the same document discusses Belo Horizonte's specific PIB share in depth.

IPEDF/CODEPLAN's own page states GDP results integrate Brazil's Sistema de Contas Regionais (an IBGE project) and that IPEDF Codeplan is IBGE's official institution for calculating the Federal District's GDP within that system. DF is coterminous with the single 'Brasilia' municipality in IBGE's municipal series.

IPECE's own 'Analise do PIB dos Municipios Cearenses -- 2022/2023' states its Municipal GDP Series 'constitui uma analise dos ultimos resultados disponiveis das Contas Regionais divulgados pelo IBGE' and that municipal GDP calculation is conceptually integrated with Brazil's Regional Accounts System procedures.

News coverage of the joint IBGE/SEPLAN-SC municipal-GDP release quotes SEPLAN-SC economist Paulo Zoldan as coordinating 'a apuracao do PIB do Estado e dos municipios em parceria com o IBGE'. Zoldan is independently confirmed as Santa Catarina's named external collaborator in IBGE's own official technical note for this same product (https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/livros/liv102250_notas_tecnicas.pdf) -- corroborating a real, direct role rather than a paraphrase.

IBGE's own official technical note for 'Produto Interno Bruto dos Municipios: Brasil: 2022-2023' names IPARDES (Instituto Paranaense de Desenvolvimento Economico e Social) as Parana's external collaborator institute for this product, with two named individual collaborators. IPARDES's own site had no quotable prose specific to the municipal series, so this edge rests on IBGE's own document rather than IPARDES's.

IBGE's own official technical note for 'Produto Interno Bruto dos Municipios: Brasil: 2022-2023' names CEPERJ (Fundacao Centro Estadual de Estatisticas, Pesquisas e Formacao de Servidores Publicos do Rio de Janeiro) as Rio de Janeiro's external collaborator institute for this product, with two named individual collaborators. CEPERJ's own domains were unreachable this round (consistent robots.txt/timeout/403 across 6+ attempts), so this edge rests on IBGE's own document rather than CEPERJ's -- same pattern as an official agency's own page standing in when the primary domain is technically unreachable.

Bihar Statistical Handbook 2020 (Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Govt of Bihar) carries recurring per-table source footnotes citing the Census of India across multiple rounds -- 'Source:- Census of India -2011 & Previous Year' and 'Source- Census Of India.' -- with 2011 named repeatedly alongside 2001/1991/1981 rounds.
Statistical Abstract of Haryana 2023-24 states explicitly (Section III, Area and Population): 'The data have been taken from the Census of India, 1961, 1971, 1981, 1991, 2001 and 2011.'

National Health Profile 2023's own 'Information to our readers' section states 'Population census- Main source of demographic data which is conducted at a decadal interval.' Direction corrected from the researching subagent's proposal (which had Census as source): NHP is the document citing Census as an input, not the reverse.

National Health Profile 2023's own 'Information to our readers' section states 'Population surveys, population projections and Sample Registration System (SRS) are other sources of demographic data.' Direction corrected from the researching subagent's proposal (which had SRS as source): NHP is the document citing SRS as an input, not the reverse.

London's own 2024-2027 Multi-Year Budget states directly: 'Tax rates are applied to the current value assessment of each property as determined by the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC), which is an independent body formed by the Provincial government and funded by municipalities.' In-document citation -- the cleanest of this round's Ontario municipal-budget findings.

Ottawa's annual 'Tax Policy and Other Revenue Matters' report (2025 edition -- the 2026 edition of the same recurring report series was inaccessible this session) states: 'Property taxes in Ontario are calculated based on assessment values determined by the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) and multiplied by the City and Province's tax rates.' Supersedes a prior no-document verdict against a different, Incapsula-blocked URL for the same underlying fact (see on-ontario-deepen-grok-2026-08.json, resolved this round).

Brampton's official Taxes & Assessment page states: 'The Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) is responsible for assessing all properties in the Province of Ontario, including the City of Brampton.' The Adopted Budget PDF itself was too large to fetch and the shorter Budget Highlights PDF had no MPAC mention, so this rests on the City's own webpage rather than the budget document proper -- same evidentiary pattern accepted for Caledon below.

Caledon's official Property Assessments page states: 'Every four years, the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) conducts a province-wide assessment and mails a Property Assessment Notice to all property owners in Ontario.' The full 2026 Budget Book exceeded fetch size limits, so this rests on the Town's own webpage rather than the budget document proper.

Halifax Regional Municipality's own Budget 'Common Questions' page states: 'PVSC is an independent, municipally funded, not-for-profit organization that provides property assessment services and information to Nova Scotia's municipalities and property owners' and 'the tax bill is made up of the assessment (set by PVSC) multiplied by the tax rate (set by the municipality).' The Budget and Business Plan PDF itself returned 403 on every attempt, so this rests on HRM's own budget-section FAQ page. Supersedes a prior no-document verdict against a different, non-matching halifax.ca URL for the same underlying fact (see atlantic-canada-grok-2026-08.json, resolved this round).

The Municipal Assessment Agency's own 2024-2025 Annual Report describes its core line of business: 'On behalf of municipalities, we provide residents and commercial property owners with real property values annually.' A self-citation from the Agency's own annual report onto its own core assessment product.

The City of Winnipeg's own tax-bill explainer states: 'To calculate the municipal tax amount, the City multiplies the portioned assessment by the municipal mill rate,' with the portioned assessment 'set at 45 percent of the assessed value of the property' and the mill rate itself 'set by City Council through the budget process.' The governing 'Real and Personal Property Municipal Tax Rate By-law' text itself was not independently fetchable (listing page only), so this rests on the City's own explainer page describing the budget-set mill rate applied to the assessment roll.

Ontario's Tuition Fee Framework Guidelines state: 'Unless otherwise indicated in these Guidelines, all policies in relation to tuition fees in the current university Ontario Operating Funds Distribution Manual remain in effect,' and define enrolment for tuition purposes as 'fiscal full-time equivalent enrolments eligible and claimed for Ministry operating grant support as defined in the Operating Funds Distribution Manual.'

Ontario's official SMA3 Performance/Outcomes-Based Funding Technical Manual, which governs postsecondary operating-grant metrics, names 'Census Data (Statistics Canada)' as the data source for its Community/Local Impact metric (parallel line for colleges via CSER).
